article.title: The Copilot+ PC brand is dead

editorial:
When an AI Label Stops Helping

Microsoft’s apparent retreat from “Copilot PC” branding says less about the future of AI hardware than about the limits of repetition. A label should tell buyers what a machine can do. When “Copilot” appears across products with different capabilities, it becomes harder to distinguish a useful feature from a marketing promise.

There is a technical story worth telling instead. Dedicated neural processors can run some models locally, potentially improving latency and keeping sensitive data off remote servers. But buyers need to know which applications benefit, how well they perform, and whether features work offline. An AI badge cannot answer those questions.

Developers face a similar test: are the APIs stable, the capabilities accessible, and the benefits large enough to justify supporting another hardware path? Clear benchmarks and practical examples would do more for adoption than a louder campaign. If the branding is fading, Microsoft has an opportunity to let measurable utility define the category.
